lesson.text: Quick memory: who keeps an orchestra together? (The conductor.) Today: rounds, songs for groups that start at different times.
In a round, everyone sings the same tune, but the groups start one after another. The lines are written so that they sound good on top of each other.
Frère Jacques is a French round, over 200 years old. In English, line 1 is: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping. Listen.
Line 2: Brother John, Brother John. Line 3: Morning bells are ringing, morning bells are ringing. Line 4: Ding, dang, dong, ding, dang, dong.
Group 2 starts line 1 when group 1 reaches line 2. With 4 lines, up to 4 groups can join, each one line later. Singing different notes at the same time makes harmony.
Tips: know the tune really well first; listen to the others, but hold on to your own line; keep the same steady beat; and stand with your group.
Sumer Is Icumen In is one of the oldest rounds known. It was written in England more than 700 years ago.
Try it in the world: sing Frère Jacques as a round with friends or family in your world's village square: one group starts, and the next joins in at line 2. Next: music long ago.

exercises.prompt: In a round, what do the groups sing?
choices: the same tune, starting at different times
exercises.explain: Every group sings the same tune, starting one after another.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which words fit this line of Frère Jacques?
exercises.hint: Count the notes: how many syllables fit? Are they quick or long?
choices: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping
exercises.explain: 8 steady notes: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping. It is line 1.

exercises.prompt: Listen to line 1 of Frère Jacques. How does it go?
exercises.hint: Draw the tune in the air with your finger as you listen.
choices: up by steps, then back down
exercises.explain: C, D, E climb by steps, then it drops back to C, and the same again.

exercises.prompt: In a round, group 2 starts after group 1 has begun.
exercises.explain: True: group 2 waits, then starts line 1 when group 1 reaches line 2.

exercises.prompt: When group 1 sings line 3, which line does group 2 sing?
exercises.hint: Find line 3 in group 1's row, then look straight down.
exercises.explain: Group 2 is one line behind: 3 − 1 = 2, line 2.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which line of Frère Jacques is this?
exercises.hint: Listen for the low bell notes.
choices: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping
exercises.explain: The low bell sounds are line 4: Ding, dang, dong.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which line of Frère Jacques is this?
choices: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping
exercises.explain: The quick notes are line 3: Morning bells are ringing.

exercises.prompt: Put the lines of Frère Jacques in order.
exercises.hint: Sing it in your head from the start.
items: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping
exercises.explain: Are you sleeping, Brother John, Morning bells are ringing, Ding, dang, dong.

exercises.prompt: Sort these tips for singing a round: do they help or not?
items: listen, but hold your own line
exercises.hint: What keeps the parts together and fitting?
exercises.explain: Knowing the tune, a steady beat and holding your line help. Shouting, joining the other line and speeding up don't.

exercises.prompt: A round has 4 lines. How many groups can sing it, each starting one line later?
exercises.hint: Each group starts one line after the one before.
exercises.explain: One group for each line: 4 groups.

exercises.prompt: Two different notes sung at the same time make harmony.
exercises.hint: What does a round give you?
exercises.explain: True: that is harmony, and a round makes it from just one tune.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which picture shows the tune of this line?
exercises.hint: Does the tune climb or fall? Where does it start again?
exercises.explain: It climbs E, F, G, then climbs again E, F, G: Brother John, Brother John.

exercises.prompt: Frère Jacques has 4 lines. 3 groups sing it once each, starting a line apart. How many lines long is the whole song?
exercises.hint: When does the last group start? It still sings all 4 lines.
exercises.explain: The third group starts 2 lines after the first and sings 4: 2 + 4 = 6 lines.

exercises.prompt: How old is Sumer Is Icumen In, one of the oldest rounds known?
exercises.explain: It was written in England more than 700 years ago.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which line of Frère Jacques has these long notes?
exercises.hint: Which words would you hold on the long notes?
choices: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping
exercises.explain: The long notes are line 2: Brother John, Brother John.

exercises.prompt: At the 4th time step, what does group 3 sing?
exercises.hint: Find group 3's row, then the 4th column.
exercises.explain: Group 3 starts at the 3rd step with line 1, so at the 4th it sings line 2.

exercises.prompt: Why do the lines of a round sound good together?
exercises.hint: Think about how a composer writes a round.
choices: they were written to fit on top of each other
exercises.explain: The lines were written to fit together when sung at the same time.

exercises.prompt: In a round, every group finishes at the same time.
exercises.explain: False: they started one after another, so they finish one after another.

exercises.prompt: Three groups sing Frère Jacques as a round, each starting one line later. At time step 3, which line is each group singing?
exercises.hint: Group 1 starts at step 1, group 2 at step 2, group 3 at step 3.
exercises.explain: Group 1 started at step 1, so at step 3 it sings line 3. Group 2 started a step later: line 2. Group 3 has just started: line 1. Three lines at once make harmony.
